I am His and He hath chosen Me,
For all those who seek the lord shall find Him ;
When I was young my heart did love to roam
Far from the home where God had set me down;

But when I found that He had sent me here
To be His servant at this tender age,

My spirit longed to return once more

author: cushag
text:
Where is she ?

When you are near, I hear her footsteps ;

For now and then the little girl does go

To wander far among our silent groves—

And oft we mark by their deep retreat

The darkling spots where men should not tread.

Ah ! well I know they are but playful toys,

But yet I am ever watchful to see

If any thing should fall from bough or brier —

Johnnie and Me Was Married

In yonder land long ago,
There lived two brothers so gay,

But oh! that dear old story—
Ah it’s not fit to say!

Both on their father’s knee,
They learned from him all good lore;

And then they grew up young men,
Then got them selves some wives afore.

And this one day there came along
A lovely lady full of grace ;

She looked as if she had danced
With Cupid in his golden place.

I love my Old man. He is tall
and broad shouldered. He has blue eyes
that look out over the sea as he stands
in his boat and looks back over his shoulder

At night when we see the stars shining so bright
He says they are all our family up above us.

text:
The sea was very dark, and he had not looked for a while at the stars; but now he turned to them with wonder.

O the glory of this great world! I cannot take it all in my heart! The sky is red—the moon has gone down behind that same red sky; there are such wonderful fires on it as if they were diamonds,—and then these strange shapes —what can they be? They go off through the air like little birds,--but they do not fly away, because they have wings of light too. O the mystery of things!

 Its silent stories old;
 My heart! Through all its days untold,
 It comes back to you,
